## REASONING

The request has two goals: (1) characterize seasonal ET dynamics across the Passaic basin, and (2) validate against eddy-covariance (EC) flux towers. The critical feasibility problem is immediate: the brief states EC flux towers are MISSING from the data stack. ET is what EC directly measures, so the validation goal as literally posed is **not answerable in-domain**. I must be honest about this and propose alternatives (indirect water-balance ET from USGS gauges; soil-moisture/water-table constraints from USGS wells) while clearly labeling them as indirect, not co-located ET validation.

The mechanistic goal IS answerable. ELM single-column resolves the surface energy/water balance and thus ET partitioning. The candidate drivers are land cover and soil — both are levers ELM can genuinely pull (PFT/vegetation and soil texture). The elevation range (3–390 m) is modest and, more importantly, with uniform forcing the stack cannot isolate any elevation/climate effect (no elevation-downscaled forcing), so I do NOT stratify on elevation as a climate axis — variation across elevation-placed columns would be confounded soil/land-cover variation. Land cover and soil are the defensible stratification axes.

N: this is a mechanistic characterization across two categorical drivers. Span dominant land-cover classes (forest, developed/urban — the Passaic is heavily urbanized, agriculture/grass, wetland) crossed with dominant soil texture classes. A full cross is not needed; I sample the realistic combinations. ~10–12 exploratory columns span the space. Validation columns are pinned to gauge subwatershed outlets and well locations — count dictated by data density, unknown here.

Indirect ET validation via streamflow requires runoff routing/aggregation the framework lacks — flagged in requires_capabilities.

  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    {"capability": "eddy-covariance flux-tower ingest", "why": "Direct ET validation as posed requires EC observations, absent in-domain.", "blocks": "the stated validation goal"},
    {"capability": "elevation-downscaled forcing", "why": "To attribute any ET variation to elevation/climate rather than confounded soil/cover.", "blocks": "elevation control on ET"},
    {"capability": "runoff routing / spatial aggregation to gauge outlets", "why": "To compare column runoff to USGS gauge streamflow and derive water-balance ET.", "blocks": "indirect streamflow-based ET validation"},
    {"capability": "USGS well data ingest + co-location resolver", "why": "To pin water-table/soil-moisture columns to well locations for indirect ET-drawdown validation.", "blocks": "well-based validation"},

  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Land-cover classes forest / developed / agriculture-grass / wetland and soil classes coarse/medium/fine are the dominant strata; actual class fractions to be resolved from rasters by the expander.",
    "Basin is not snow-dominated (max 390 m), so snow is a minor ET/partitioning control here.",
    "USGS gauges and wells have some in-domain density, but exact counts/locations are unknown at design time.",
    "A representative baseline forcing period within 1980-2018 is used uniformly across columns."
  ],
  "open_questions": [
    "Is any eddy-covariance tower available outside the domain in an analogous NJ/mid-Atlantic setting for analog ET validation?",
    "What is the in-domain density and record length of USGS gauges and wells?",

    "Which analysis window(s) within 1980-2018 are of interest (recent climatology vs full record)?"
  ]
}
